title: refactor(scripts): the item-carrier disposition is RULED and says it is not a dialect
body:
Fixes #9871

`Clause-②: no` — an internal scanner's disposition string and the pins that read it. It moves no exported symbol and no key on a published payload.

## What this is

The second flight on objectui#9871. The first one's code landed (PR #9940, `Part of` on purpose, while the family question was still open). The director seat then answered it — **summon #25 class-1 item 2, letter C**, 2026-09-20:

> A `body` child list on a non-node ITEM (tab item, list item) is ⛔ not inside objectui#6771's ruled family and ⛔ not a second family: it is a producer violating the item's published schema, fixed at the producer (done: objectui#9941). The scanner's `unruled:item-carrier` disposition is renamed to a ruled, non-dialect disposition … and leaves any pending list; objectui#6771 step 4's landability is judged on the node face only.

This PR is that rename and its pins. ⛔ The scan, the criterion and the census are ⛔ not re-opened.

## The spelling, and why it is not neutral

`dispositionOf('item')` is now **`ruled:not-a-dialect/item-schema-violation`**.

The name carries the answer rather than leaving a reader to guess it, and the ruling is cited **where a reader MEETS the disposition**, not only in the file header:

- beside the constant (`dispositionOf`'s docblock);
- in the `KNOWN_LIMITS` entry — id `unruled-item-carrier` becomes `item-carrier-not-in-ruled-total` — which **every run emits in both output modes**;
- in the note the text mode prints under the dispositions table.

Each of those three states in one line what the site actually IS: a producer violating the item's own published schema (`TabItemSchema` declares `content` and declares no `body`; `ListItem` likewise), fixed at the producer.

## The behavioural half, which is not a string

- **It leaves every pending list.** The header section「The open question this scan REPORTS and ⛔ does not answer」is gone; its replacement states the ruling. The `KNOWN_LIMITS` entry no longer says「unruled … reports the question rather than answering it」, and the printed note no longer asks it. An `item` hit awaits no seat.
- **The arithmetic did ⛔ NOT change.** An item carrier is still never folded into objectui#6771's ruled total. What changed is the reason — not that family at all, rather than not-yet-judged.
- **Step 4 landability: already right, ⛔ not "fixed".** Read before changing, as the order required: the scan does ⛔ not compute or report objectui#6771 step 4's landability. `finalVerdict`'s docblock already disclaimed it in as many words (「It is NOT … the day objectui#6771 step 4 becomes landable」), and item carriers were already out of the ruled bucket. Only the prose moved, to state the node-face-only rule.

## ⚠️ The hazard this rename introduces, pinned in the same act

Both answers now begin `ruled:`. A reader that bucketed on that **prefix** would fold the item carrier straight into the ruled total — the one arithmetic the ruling says must not weaken. The discriminator is the **carrier**, never the prefix, and a new pin holds the two buckets apart on exactly that (`new Set(byDisposition).size` is 2 while both rows start `ruled:`).

## Evidence

**RED before / GREEN after, file state proved in the SAME command.** The pins were written first and run against the byte-identical scanner: worktree blob `b51f13aaa` == `HEAD:scripts/body-dialect-producer-scan.mjs` `b51f13aaa`, and the run failed **4 of 26** — `expected 'unruled:item-carrier' to be 'ruled:not-a-dialect/item-schema-viola…'`, the two-bucket equality, the `KNOWN_LIMITS` id lookup (`expected undefined to be truthy`) and the CLI payload's id list. After the scanner change, blob `d42f6ac95` != HEAD: **2 files, 48 tests passed**.

**The scan itself, before and after, both buckets lit.** On a planted corpus carrying BOTH carriers in one run, so the split is a discrimination and not an artifact of a one-shaped corpus:

| disposition | before | after |
|:--|--:|--:|
| `ruled:6771` (node, the control) | 1 | 1 |
| `unruled:item-carrier` | 1 | — |
| `ruled:not-a-dialect/item-schema-violation` | — | 1 |

On the **live tree**, nothing moved and nothing was supposed to: 0 producers before and after, with the same-subject controls identical in both runs — 5,189 files scanned, 1,067 candidate `body` spellings, 312 held out by C2, 5 passing C2 with no recognised emission channel. ⭐ Those controls are the point: a zero from a corpus that could not have held the subject would be a broken instrument, and this card exists because a classifier was provably blind in two directions.

**Premise re-taken before any edit**, on `origin/main` `0c2eb5eee`, each leg with its control in the same command: the criterion header carries `C1 — EMISSION` / `C2 — RESOLUTION` / `C3 — CARRIER`; `unruled:item-carrier` was present at 8 sites in 3 files while the control spelling `ruled:6771` lit 4 sites in the same command (so the instrument distinguishes *this* spelling from *any* disposition); the shipped `tabs` `defaultProps` spell `content`, objectui#9941 is closed, and the producer-side repair the ruling rests on really is landed.

**Gates, re-run as the last action before the push**, at `5d81f6cda` with `git diff HEAD` empty and nothing untracked: `check:control-bytes`, `check:entry-guard`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:comment-mask-corpus`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:changeset-presence`, `check-hand-rolled-comment-mask`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:lint-rule-coverage`, `check:required-check-set --self-test` — all exit 0. Tests behind the shared verify lock (`VERDICT command-exit 0`).

**Changeset: decided by the gate, ⛔ not from memory.** `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` at `5d81f6cda`: `No source or published contract of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed.` (3 files changed, 0 of them published source.)

**ESLint narrowing, declared with its three readings** at `5d81f6cda`: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 3 changed files — ② the JSON carries 3 file entries, 0 errors, 0 warnings; ① the population is read from `eslint.config.js` itself, whose 471 lines configure no type-aware linting (`projectService` / `parserOptions` / `project:` grep exits 1, with `languageOptions` / `rules:` lit as the control in the same command); ③ therefore this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` run is CI's.

## Acceptance notes

⛔ No third file reads the disposition string. The census pin `scripts/__tests__/body-dialect-census.test.ts` is one of the scanner's pins under `scripts/__tests__/` and is inside the declared surface; `package.json` and `.changeset/9871-body-dialect-producer-scan.md` name the *script*, never the disposition, and are untouched.

⚠️ The census pin's item-carrier assertion stays **vacuous on the live tree** — the item-carried set has been empty since objectui#9941, so the loop body never runs. It is updated to the new spelling and kept, ⛔ not deleted, exactly as its own comment instructs: it fires the moment an item-carried producer returns. The instrument that actually failed before this change is the producer-scan pin set, which is where the new assertions live.

`noted, not filed:` `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/tabs.tsx` still reads `item.content || (item as any).body` — a lenient consumer fallback for the spelling the producer no longer emits. It is a **reader**, so the criterion correctly scores it as not a producer, and it is also what keeps C2's item leg resolvable. Retiring it is a consumer-side decision on the item face, ⛔ not this card's rename, and ⛔ not a dialect question under the ruling above. Successor: whoever holds the item face on objectui#9590.
